question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
device: rolling-element bearing in a 350 kW industrial fan drive
failure: inner-race spalling progresses for weeks before the vibration alarm trips; by then the bearing is past repair
followup_finding: We re-analyzed the last 12 months: bearing fault-frequency harmonics appear 19 days before the alarm in our worst case, and the 80th percentile was 16 days. The 5 dB band above BPFI sidebands overlaps with the gearbox defect signature.
constraint: predictor must use existing 1 kHz vibration sensor and 1 Hz SCADA logging only, fire at least 14 days warning, produce no more than 2 false alarms per year
user_variables: at most 2 false alarms per year
round1_answer:
UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESIS — this candidate was NOT endorsed by the adversarial gauntlet (it was revised once and rejected again). It is delivered as a hypothesis requiring the falsification test below; it is NOT an invention claim.

stress distributions in composite structures evaluated through finite element simulations and analytical frameworks

Use the 1 kHz vibration sensor to isolate BPFI sidebands, filtering out the overlapping 80th percentile gearbox defect signature via a spectral subtraction model based on the 19-day harmonic appearance window.

Detection of bearing fault-frequency harmonics 19 days before the traditional alarm trips, reducing false alarms caused by gearbox noise overlap to <2 per year.

Run a spectral analysis on 12 months of historical data; verify that the isolated BPFI component precedes the SCADA vibration threshold crossing by at least 16 days in 80% of failure cases, and that the residual spectrum after subtracting the modeled gearbox signature remains below the 5 dB noise floor.
